body.statement: Uniformly over \(P\in\mathfrak P^{\mathrm{pred}}_{n,m}(r,\mu,K,q,B,\lambda)\) in regimes with \(b_{nm}=o(1)\), recorded-propensity IPW-SVD satisfies \(\mathcal L(\widehat U^{\mathrm I},U)=O_P(b_{nm})\). This maximum-row claim is pointwise in the target and contains no factor depending on \(|\mathcal G_n|\).
body.justification: This is the calibrated martingale maximum-row recovery theorem.
body.gap: Mehrotra et al., public Algorithm 1, Theorem 3.2, and Corollary 3.3 in Section 3, attain the same geometric rowwise matrix-error scale using armwise empirical-row-scaled SVD under independent Bernoulli assignments, unknown propensities, and low-rankness of each arm mean. That result neither permits history-predictable assignments nor studies the left singular space of an effect matrix when the two arm means themselves may be high rank. Cai et al., published Assumptions 1--2 on page 948 and Theorem 1, equations (16b)--(17) on page 950, require independent Bernoulli entries and independent noise for a diagonal-deleted Gram estimator. Han et al., published equation (1) on page 1964 and Theorem 2.2 on page 1974, prove a Frobenius-rate online SGD result for independent Gaussian matrix contexts. Athey et al., published Assumptions 1--2 and Theorem 2, equation (14), on pages 1720 and 1724, and Sun et al., published equation (1), Assumptions 1--3, equation (11), and Theorem 3 in Sections 2--4 of article e70002, control outcome-matrix Frobenius errors rather than predictable causal-effect row-subspace loss.
body.consumer: HeartSteps II analysts can recover latent response profiles without treating personalized probabilities as independent.
